one_liner: Sherlock (sherlock-project) is a local open-source Python CLI for username enumeration across sites; it has no hosted HTTP API or credentials, so it can't become a standard hosted-API toolkit.
auth_notes: The repo page shows a local CLI invoked as `sherlock user123` with no login, key or token options in its help output. Other products named Sherlock (Aleph Alpha Pharia Sherlock, shebang's sherlock auth, Sherlock MCP for .NET, CodeSherlock) are unrelated.
access_notes: The MIT-licensed CLI installs for free with pipx, pip, uv or Docker, with no account. There is no vendor-hosted service to get credentials for.
blocker_notes: It is a local CLI with no hosted API; a toolkit would have to run the CLI itself. The draft's community MCP (Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp) does not appear in any fetched page, so it is not confirmed. The MCP servers that do appear (Sherlock MCP for .NET, CodeSherlock, shebang) are different products. The vendor-namespace MCP registry search found nothing.
